doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Jump Town and the Ventura band
title: The live fade-out and the big-band album with Quincy Jones
summary: The fade-out ending on 'Bubbles', the later Creed Taylor big-band album with arrangements by Quincy Jones, Ernie Wilkins, Ralph Burns, Bill Holman and Roy.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I wanted to ask about the fade out section on “I’m Forever Blowing Bubbles.” I was taking notes while you were playing.
Good. That’s called doing your homework.
It’s easy once you get it.
She would start and then I answer, and it kept alternating.

But originally it wasn’t that way. Originally we had a set ending, and it was sort of in harmony with the horn and when we did it with Charlie. But then later on we re-recorded it because I think it was Creed Taylor wanted us to do it again. And we did an album with a big band, you know. It was a great time because we did it with was it—
Quincy Jones was the conductor and he did a couple of the arrangements, but we were using it as an arranger’s showcase. We had Ernie Wilkins wrote two, Roy wrote two, Quincy wrote two—
Ralph Burns wrote the ballads. And it was really nice.
And Bill Holman did a couple of vocalese things.

Bill Holman did two. And so it was a fun album for us because it got us out of doing the same thing, and you know you like to change what you’re doing. It makes it more interesting, more exciting. And so when we did that Ernie Wilkins wrote the arrangement and at the end he changed it. He thought it would be more effective for a record. Because it’s easy to do a fade out.
On the board you know. But when we started doing it again, we said well let’s do it that way. It’s kind of a fun ending, but it’s hard to do a fade out.
But people get it, especially if you don’t use it for your last tune. It doesn’t evoke a lot of applause maybe right away.
